mechanism: NSAIDs reduce prostaglandin-mediated renal perfusion, worsening GFR and causing fluid/sodium retention and hyperkalaemia.
recommendation: Avoid in moderate-to-severe CKD; if unavoidable use the lowest dose briefly with renal monitoring.

mechanism: Sodium and fluid retention plus reduced renal perfusion can precipitate decompensation and blunt diuretic effect.
recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs in heart failure; use paracetamol for analgesia.

mechanism: COX-1 inhibition impairs gastroprotective prostaglandins, increasing ulceration and GI bleeding risk.
recommendation: Avoid in active or prior peptic ulcer disease; if essential, co-prescribe a proton-pump inhibitor.

mechanism: Reduced renal clearance causes metformin accumulation, raising the risk of lactic acidosis.
recommendation: Withhold metformin in AKI and in severe CKD (eGFR <30); reassess before restarting.

mechanism: Tissue hypoperfusion/hypoxia in acute decompensation increases lactic acidosis risk.
recommendation: Avoid during acute decompensation/hypoxia; stable chronic heart failure with preserved renal function is not a contraindication.

mechanism: Beta-2 blockade can precipitate severe bronchospasm.
recommendation: Avoid non-selective beta-blockers in asthma; a cardioselective agent may be used cautiously when strongly indicated.

mechanism: Foetotoxic in the 2nd/3rd trimester — oligohydramnios, renal dysgenesis, skull defects.
recommendation: Stop ACE inhibitors/ARBs before or as soon as pregnancy is confirmed; switch to a pregnancy-safe antihypertensive (e.g. labetalol, methyldopa, nifedipine).

mechanism: Reduced aldosterone lowers potassium excretion, worsening hyperkalaemia.
recommendation: Avoid starting in significant hyperkalaemia; monitor potassium and renal function after initiation/dose change.

mechanism: Aldosterone antagonism reduces potassium excretion, risking dangerous hyperkalaemia, especially with CKD or RAAS inhibitors.
recommendation: Avoid in significant hyperkalaemia or severe renal impairment; monitor potassium closely.

mechanism: Inadequate urinary concentration when eGFR is low reduces efficacy and increases systemic toxicity.
recommendation: Avoid if eGFR <45 mL/min (short-course use with caution at 30–44 may be considered per local guidance).

mechanism: Oxidant stress can precipitate acute haemolysis in G6PD-deficient patients.
recommendation: Avoid in known G6PD deficiency; choose an alternative urinary antimicrobial.

mechanism: Causes fluid retention that can precipitate or worsen heart failure.
recommendation: Do not use in heart failure or a history of heart failure.

mechanism: 5-HT1B-mediated vasoconstriction can provoke coronary spasm and ischaemia.
recommendation: Avoid triptans in established ischaemic heart disease, uncontrolled hypertension or prior MI.

mechanism: Central D2 antagonism worsens parkinsonian motor symptoms and antagonises dopaminergic therapy.
recommendation: Avoid in Parkinson disease; use domperidone (peripheral D2 antagonist) or ondansetron for nausea.

mechanism: Associated with increased risk of stroke and all-cause mortality in older people with dementia.
recommendation: Avoid routine use; reserve for severe distress/risk at the lowest dose for the shortest time after non-drug measures.

condition: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
mechanism: Negative inotropy can worsen systolic heart failure.
recommendation: Avoid verapamil/diltiazem in HFrEF; use a heart-failure-indicated beta-blocker for rate control.

mechanism: Oestrogen further raises the already-increased ischaemic stroke risk in migraine with aura.
recommendation: Avoid combined hormonal contraception; offer progestogen-only or non-hormonal methods.

references.label: UK/WHO Medical Eligibility Criteria for Contraceptive Use

mechanism: Oestrogen increases venous thromboembolism risk.
recommendation: Avoid in current or prior VTE; use progestogen-only or non-hormonal contraception.

mechanism: Potential hepatotoxicity; transaminases may rise.
recommendation: Avoid starting in active liver disease or unexplained persistent transaminase elevation >3x ULN; recheck LFTs.

mechanism: Starting urate-lowering therapy during a flare can prolong or worsen it by mobilising urate.
recommendation: Do not start allopurinol during an acute flare; begin once settled, under anti-inflammatory cover. If already established, continue through the flare.

mechanism: Unopposed alpha-adrenergic stimulation can precipitate a hypertensive crisis.
recommendation: Never give a beta-blocker before adequate alpha-blockade in phaeochromocytoma.

mechanism: Further suppression of AV conduction and heart rate can cause haemodynamic collapse.
recommendation: Avoid in second/third-degree AV block (without pacemaker) or symptomatic bradycardia.

mechanism: Immunosuppression can worsen or mask infection (including reactivation of TB or strongyloidiasis).
recommendation: Use with caution; treat/exclude serious infection, screen for latent TB/strongyloides before prolonged high-dose therapy.

mechanism: Further QT prolongation increases the risk of torsades de pointes.
recommendation: Avoid in congenital/acquired long QT; correct electrolytes and review concomitant QT-prolonging drugs.

mechanism: COX-1 inhibition impairs gastric mucosal defence (prostaglandin-mediated mucus and bicarbonate secretion) and adds an antiplatelet bleeding effect; precipitates ulcer recurrence and bleeding.
recommendation: Avoid aspirin in active or recent peptic ulcer disease. If antiplatelet therapy is required for vascular indication, eradicate H. pylori, use a PPI, and consider clopidogrel only after specialist review.

references.label: ACG Guideline — peptic ulcer disease; BNF

condition: Aspirin-exacerbated respiratory disease (Samter triad) / known NSAID-sensitive asthma
mechanism: COX-1 inhibition shifts arachidonic acid metabolism toward cysteinyl leukotrienes, precipitating bronchospasm in susceptible asthmatics (especially with nasal polyposis).
recommendation: Avoid aspirin and non-selective NSAIDs. Use paracetamol; if NSAID essential, consider a selective COX-2 inhibitor under specialist guidance with desensitisation if vascular indication.

references.label: GINA Asthma guidance; EAACI position paper on AERD

drug: Macrolide antibiotics (erythromycin, clarithromycin, azithromycin to a lesser degree)
mechanism: hERG (Ikr) potassium channel blockade prolongs cardiac repolarisation; risk of torsades de pointes amplified by congenital LQTS, hypokalaemia, hypomagnesaemia, bradycardia or other QT-prolonging agents.
recommendation: Avoid macrolides (especially erythromycin and clarithromycin). Choose a non-QT-prolonging alternative (doxycycline, amoxicillin, β-lactam per indication).

references.label: CredibleMeds QT drug list; ESC LQTS management

mechanism: Oxidative stress can precipitate acute haemolysis in G6PD-deficient red cells, particularly during infection.
recommendation: Use with caution; prefer a non-oxidant antibiotic where appropriate. If used, monitor haemoglobin and haptoglobin and advise patient to seek care for jaundice, dark urine or pallor.

references.label: WHO Guide to G6PD deficiency in drug prescribing

mechanism: Strong oxidants — predictable haemolysis in G6PD-deficient erythrocytes, sometimes severe enough to require transfusion.
recommendation: Avoid in G6PD deficiency. Choose a non-oxidant alternative (e.g. pentamidine or atovaquone for PCP; macrolide or β-lactam for UTI per local susceptibility).

condition: Insulin-treated diabetes with hypoglycaemia awareness reliance
mechanism: Blunts adrenergic warning symptoms of hypoglycaemia (tremor, tachycardia, palpitations) and inhibits gluconeogenesis; prolongs and masks hypoglycaemia.
recommendation: Prefer cardioselective β1-blockers (bisoprolol, metoprolol) at the lowest effective dose in insulin-treated diabetes; counsel patient about altered symptoms.

condition: Epilepsy / lowered seizure threshold (eating disorders, alcohol withdrawal)
mechanism: Dose-dependent reduction in seizure threshold (incidence 0.1–0.4% at therapeutic doses, much higher above maximum recommended dose).
recommendation: Do NOT prescribe in seizure disorders, current/past anorexia or bulimia, or during alcohol/benzodiazepine withdrawal. Choose an alternative antidepressant or smoking-cessation aid.

references.label: FDA label for bupropion; NICE depression guideline

condition: Chronic kidney disease (eGFR < 60 mL/min) or AKI
mechanism: Renally excreted with narrow therapeutic index; reduced clearance precipitates lithium toxicity. Long-term lithium itself can cause nephrogenic diabetes insipidus and progressive CKD.
recommendation: Avoid initiating in significant CKD; if already established, reduce dose and monitor lithium level + U&E every 1–3 months. Hold during AKI or dehydration.

condition: Pregnancy / women of childbearing potential without effective contraception
mechanism: Major teratogen — neural tube defects (1–2%), cardiac and craniofacial malformations, plus long-term neurodevelopmental disability (autism, lower IQ) in up to 30–40% of exposed children.
recommendation: Do NOT prescribe to women of childbearing potential unless no alternative AND a pregnancy-prevention programme is in place (MHRA Valproate PPP). Switch to lamotrigine or levetiracetam when planning pregnancy.

references.label: MHRA Valproate Pregnancy Prevention Programme (2018); WHO Essential Medicines warnings

mechanism: Lithium use in the first trimester is associated with cardiac malformations (Ebstein anomaly) — historically estimated ~1:1000 absolute risk above baseline; later trimesters risk neonatal toxicity and floppy-baby.
recommendation: Avoid where possible in the first trimester. If essential for severe bipolar disorder, use the lowest effective dose, monitor levels closely, perform fetal echocardiography at 16–20 weeks, plan delivery with neonatal/maternal teams.

references.label: NICE Bipolar disorder in pregnancy guideline; BNF

mechanism: Modest teratogenicity — neural tube defects (~1%), craniofacial and cardiac malformations; vitamin K-dependent factor deficiency in the neonate.
recommendation: Prefer lamotrigine or levetiracetam in women of childbearing potential. If carbamazepine remains essential, give high-dose folate (5 mg/day) pre-conception, monitor closely, and give vitamin K 10 mg PO to mother in the last month + 1 mg IM to neonate at birth.

references.label: NICE Epilepsy in pregnancy; UK Epilepsy and Pregnancy Register

mechanism: Major teratogen and abortifacient — folate antagonism causes craniofacial, limb and CNS malformations (methotrexate embryopathy).
recommendation: Absolute contraindication. Stop at least 3 months before attempting conception (longer per some guidance) in both women and men. Use effective contraception during therapy. Therapeutic use in pregnancy is restricted to ectopic pregnancy and termination protocols.

references.label: EULAR points to consider for prescribing in pregnancy (2016); FDA label

mechanism: Renal elimination is the dominant clearance route; reduced clearance produces myelosuppression, mucositis and hepatotoxicity, and impairs subsequent folinic acid rescue if needed.
recommendation: Avoid methotrexate in eGFR < 30. In eGFR 30–60 use reduced dose, monitor FBC and LFT weekly initially, ensure folate 5 mg weekly (taken on a different day).

mechanism: Statins block cholesterol biosynthesis required for fetal development (steroidogenesis, neural tissue); animal teratogenicity, limited human safety data.
recommendation: Discontinue at least 1 month before conception or as soon as pregnancy is confirmed; avoid during breastfeeding. Focus on lifestyle until delivery and end of breastfeeding, then resume.

references.label: FDA pregnancy labelling; NICE familial hypercholesterolaemia guideline

mechanism: Tetracyclines chelate calcium in developing teeth and bone, causing permanent tooth discolouration and (less commonly) transient bone-growth depression with prolonged courses.
recommendation: Avoid prolonged courses in children < 8 years and in pregnancy after the first trimester. Short courses (≤21 days) of doxycycline are now considered acceptable in younger children for life-threatening rickettsial disease and severe respiratory infection per CDC (2018 update).

references.label: CDC Yellow Book; AAP Red Book

mechanism: Cartilage and tendon toxicity in juvenile animal models; rare tendinitis / tendon rupture in humans (Achilles tendon, especially with corticosteroid co-treatment).
recommendation: Reserve for serious infections (complicated UTI / pyelonephritis, multidrug-resistant TB second-line, pseudomonas-coverage in cystic fibrosis) when no safer alternative exists. Counsel about tendon symptoms and avoid concomitant systemic steroids.

references.label: FDA fluoroquinolone safety communications; AAP Red Book

condition: Children under 12 years (and 12–18 years post-tonsillectomy/adenoidectomy or with OSA / obesity)
mechanism: Codeine is bioactivated to morphine by CYP2D6. Ultra-rapid metabolisers (1–7% of European, up to 30% of North African ancestry) produce excess morphine, with reports of fatal respiratory depression in children.
recommendation: Do NOT use codeine or tramadol in children <12 years for any indication, and in any child after tonsillectomy/adenoidectomy. Choose paracetamol/ibuprofen first, then weight-appropriate morphine if needed.

references.label: FDA Drug Safety Communication (2017); EMA recommendation (2013); WHO Pain Ladder review

mechanism: Maternal CYP2D6 ultra-rapid metabolism can yield high morphine concentrations in breast milk; reports of neonatal apnoea and death.
recommendation: Avoid codeine and tramadol while breastfeeding. Use paracetamol ± ibuprofen; if opioid required, low-dose morphine or fentanyl is preferred and the infant should be observed for sedation.

references.label: FDA Drug Safety Communication (2017); UK Specialist Pharmacy Service

mechanism: Prostaglandin inhibition causes oligohydramnios, premature closure of the ductus arteriosus and fetal renal impairment after 20 weeks. Risk increases after 30 weeks.
recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs after 20 weeks. Use paracetamol; if anti-inflammatory required (severe inflammatory arthritis), specialist-supervised low-dose short course only.

references.label: FDA Drug Safety Communication (2020); NICE Antenatal Care

mechanism: Renal elimination of unchanged bisphosphonate; IV zoledronate in renal impairment is associated with acute tubular necrosis. Oral bisphosphonates lack efficacy and safety data in advanced CKD.
recommendation: Avoid bisphosphonates when eGFR < 30–35 mL/min. Treat CKD-MBD per KDIGO; in CKD G4–5 use denosumab with vigilant calcium monitoring or refer to nephrology / metabolic bone.

references.label: KDIGO CKD-MBD guideline; FDA prescribing information for zoledronate

drug: Anticholinergic / antimuscarinic agents (oxybutynin, tolterodine, amitriptyline, first-generation antihistamines)
condition: Benign prostatic hyperplasia with bladder outflow obstruction
mechanism: Blockade of bladder detrusor muscarinic (M3) receptors reduces contractility; in significant outflow obstruction this precipitates acute urinary retention.
recommendation: Avoid where bladder outflow obstruction is suspected (high IPSS, large residual volume). If overactive bladder symptoms must be treated, consider mirabegron (β3-agonist) or refer urology.

references.label: BNF; EAU Non-neurogenic Male LUTS guideline

drug: Anticholinergic / antimuscarinic agents, tricyclic antidepressants, certain antiemetics (cyclizine), first-generation antihistamines
mechanism: Pupillary dilatation crowds the iridocorneal angle in eyes with anatomically narrow angles, precipitating acute angle-closure with rapid intraocular pressure rise and visual loss.
recommendation: Avoid in narrow-angle glaucoma. Open-angle glaucoma is not a contraindication.

references.label: BNF cautions; American Academy of Ophthalmology Primary Angle Closure PPP

condition: Uncontrolled hypertension, ischaemic heart disease, severe coronary artery disease
mechanism: α-adrenergic vasoconstriction raises blood pressure and afterload; reported myocardial infarction and hypertensive crisis in susceptible patients.
recommendation: Avoid systemic decongestants; advise saline nasal irrigation, topical decongestant (≤3 days) or intranasal steroid. Counsel patients on warfarin / MAOI about specific interactions.

condition: Children < 1 year (all uses) and routine use in young adults (extrapyramidal risk)
mechanism: Dopamine D2 blockade crosses the immature BBB readily, increasing the risk of acute dystonic reactions and tardive dyskinesia, particularly with prolonged or repeated use.
recommendation: Do NOT use in children < 1 year. In children 1–18 years and young adults, limit to short courses (≤5 days), use 0.1–0.15 mg/kg/dose to a maximum of 30 mg/day, and only for nausea/vomiting refractory to first-line treatment.

references.label: EMA review of metoclopramide (2013); BNF for Children

condition: Ischaemic heart disease, uncontrolled hypertension, peripheral vascular disease, sepsis
mechanism: Potent vasoconstriction (α-adrenergic and 5-HT1) can precipitate coronary or peripheral vascular ischaemia; ergotism with prolonged or co-administered CYP3A4 inhibitor use.
recommendation: Avoid in ischaemic / vascular disease. For migraine, prefer triptans (with their own cardiovascular cautions) or non-vasoconstrictive options (gepants where available, paracetamol/NSAID). For postpartum haemorrhage, use oxytocin first-line; reserve methylergometrine where appropriate, monitoring BP.

references.label: BNF; ACOG Postpartum Haemorrhage; WHO recommendations on prevention and treatment of PPH

mechanism: Sodium / fluid retention and reduced renal perfusion may worsen decompensation; cardiovascular risk in COX-2 use is established.
recommendation: Avoid in heart failure; if essential use lowest dose for shortest period with monitoring.

references.label: ESC heart failure guideline; BNF; NICE

condition: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
mechanism: Class IC antiarrhythmics increase mortality in structural heart disease (CAST trial).
recommendation: Avoid in HFrEF or significant structural heart disease; use class III (amiodarone) where rhythm control needed.

references.label: ESC arrhythmia guideline; BNF; CAST trial

condition: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
mechanism: Class IC antiarrhythmics increase mortality in structural heart disease.
recommendation: Avoid in HFrEF or significant structural heart disease.

condition: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
mechanism: Negative inotropy worsens systolic function and may precipitate decompensation.
recommendation: Avoid in HFrEF. May be used in HFpEF with caution if other AF rate control unsuitable.

condition: Heart failure with reduced ejection fraction
mechanism: Negative inotropy worsens systolic function.
recommendation: Avoid in HFrEF; can be used in HFpEF if beta-blocker not tolerated.

mechanism: PDE-3 inhibitors increase mortality in heart failure (analogous to milrinone long-term data).
recommendation: Contraindicated in any severity of heart failure per label.

condition: Heart failure (NYHA III-IV or recent decompensation)
mechanism: PALLAS / ANDROMEDA trials showed increased mortality in severe HF.
recommendation: Avoid in NYHA III-IV heart failure or recent decompensation; avoid in permanent AF.

references.label: ESC AF guideline; BNF; ANDROMEDA trial

mechanism: SAVOR-TIMI 53 showed increased HF hospitalisations with saxagliptin.
recommendation: Avoid in established heart failure; prefer SGLT2 inhibitor or alternative DPP-4 inhibitor.

mechanism: EXAMINE showed numerical excess HF hospitalisations.
recommendation: Use with caution in heart failure; prefer SGLT2 inhibitor where appropriate.

mechanism: Thiazolidinedione causes sodium / fluid retention and increased HF risk.
recommendation: Contraindicated in NYHA I-IV heart failure.

mechanism: TNF blockade may worsen heart failure (ATTACH trial).
recommendation: Avoid in NYHA III-IV HF; use with caution in NYHA I-II with echocardiographic monitoring.

mechanism: Negative inotropy reported; FDA boxed warning.
recommendation: Contraindicated for onychomycosis / non-life-threatening indications in HF; weigh risk-benefit in invasive fungal infection.

mechanism: Renal accumulation increases nephrotoxicity and ototoxicity risk.
recommendation: Reduce dose / extend interval; TDM mandatory; avoid where alternative agents adequate.

mechanism: Nephro- and ototoxicity in renal impairment.
recommendation: TDM-guided dosing; prefer once-daily regimen with extended interval; consider alternative agent.

mechanism: Renal accumulation; ototoxicity.
recommendation: TDM-guided dosing with extended interval.

mechanism: Antianabolic effect raises urea / worsens uraemia; nephrotoxicity reported.
recommendation: Avoid tetracyclines in advanced CKD (doxycycline is the preferred alternative — eliminated faecally).

mechanism: Renal clearance; nephrotoxicity especially with concurrent piperacillin-tazobactam.
recommendation: TDM-guided dosing (trough or AUC); adjust interval; consider teicoplanin alternative.

mechanism: Contrast-associated AKI risk in CKD, diabetes, volume depletion.
recommendation: Use lowest dose iso/low-osmolar contrast; pre-hydrate (IV saline); avoid nephrotoxic combinations; consider non-contrast imaging.

mechanism: Risk of nephrogenic systemic fibrosis with linear / high-risk gadolinium agents.
recommendation: Avoid high-risk linear agents in eGFR <30; macrocyclic agents at lowest dose if essential.

mechanism: Glycaemic efficacy diminishes at low eGFR; renoprotective effect persists down to eGFR 20–25 in trials.
recommendation: Initiate per label-specified eGFR thresholds (commonly ≥20–25); avoid in dialysis. Continue cardiorenal protection while ongoing.

mechanism: Reduced renal clearance increases bleeding risk; limited dialysis data.
recommendation: Dose reduce to 2.5 mg BD if meeting two of: age ≥80, weight ≤60 kg, serum creatinine ≥133 µmol/L. Avoid in CrCl <15 unless specialist input.

mechanism: Reduced clearance.
recommendation: For NVAF: reduce to 15 mg OD if CrCl 15–49; avoid <15. For VTE: avoid <15.

mechanism: Predominantly renally cleared; accumulation causes bleeding.
recommendation: Contraindicated at CrCl <30 in UK label; reduce dose at 30–49 and avoid in elderly with risk factors.

condition: Severe renal impairment (CrCl <15) and high CrCl
mechanism: Reduced efficacy in stroke prevention at CrCl >95 in AF; bleeding risk if CrCl very low.
recommendation: Reduce dose to 30 mg OD if CrCl 15–50, weight ≤60 kg, or potent P-gp inhibitor co-prescribed. Avoid in CrCl <15. Avoid in NVAF if CrCl >95 (efficacy reduction).

mechanism: Active metabolites (M6G, M3G) accumulate causing prolonged sedation, neurotoxicity, respiratory depression.
recommendation: Avoid in eGFR <30; use oxycodone or fentanyl with dose adjustment, or alternative analgesic strategy.

mechanism: Active metabolite (morphine) accumulates.
recommendation: Avoid or reduce dose with extended interval; alternative analgesics preferred.

mechanism: Renal accumulation narrows therapeutic window; toxicity risk.
recommendation: Reduce dose (e.g. start 62.5–125 µg OD); TDM (trough 6-12 h post-dose; target 0.5-2 nmol/L in AF).

mechanism: Renal clearance; nephrogenic diabetes insipidus and CKD progression with chronic use.
recommendation: Avoid in significant CKD; specialist input if essential; close TDM; monitor eGFR 6-monthly.

mechanism: Renal clearance; accumulation causes sedation, ataxia, myoclonus, respiratory depression.
recommendation: Reduce dose per CrCl bands (e.g. 200-700 mg/day at CrCl 30-50; further reductions below). Avoid combination with opioids.

mechanism: Renal clearance.
recommendation: Reduce dose per CrCl bands; avoid combination with opioids; monitor for sedation.

mechanism: Hypersensitivity / hypotension risk; iron overload over time.
recommendation: Use per renal anaemia protocol (TSAT, ferritin targets); resuscitation facilities for infusion reactions.

mechanism: Dual RAAS blockade increases AKI, hyperkalaemia, hypotension without mortality benefit (ONTARGET / ALTITUDE).
recommendation: Do not combine ACE inhibitor with ARB; avoid combinations with direct renin inhibitor in CKD/diabetes.

mechanism: Combined RAAS / aldosterone blockade raises serum potassium.
recommendation: Check baseline K+ and eGFR; monitor at 1 and 4 weeks then 3-monthly; avoid in K+ >5.0 or eGFR <30 except specialist HF settings.

mechanism: Combined pre-glomerular and efferent arteriolar effects with diuretic volume depletion → AKI.
recommendation: Avoid the triple combination; if NSAID essential, hold diuretic during intercurrent illness; counsel on sick-day rules.

mechanism: Carbonic anhydrase inhibition alkalinises urine and reduces citrate, promoting calcium phosphate stones.
recommendation: Avoid in recurrent stone formers; increase fluid intake if used; monitor.

mechanism: Carbonic anhydrase inhibition predisposes to stones.
recommendation: Avoid in stone formers; ensure hydration.

mechanism: Reduced glutathione stores increase toxic metabolite (NAPQI) susceptibility; lowered hepatic reserve.
recommendation: Reduce maximum dose to 2-3 g/day (500 mg-1 g QDS) in chronic liver disease; avoid in active hepatitis / cirrhosis with chronic alcohol use.

references.label: BNF Appendix 2; NICE / AASLD cirrhosis guidance

mechanism: Increased risk of variceal bleeding, hepatorenal syndrome, and fluid retention in ascites.
recommendation: Avoid NSAIDs in cirrhosis; use paracetamol (reduced dose) for analgesia.

mechanism: Active liver disease is a label contraindication; benefit unclear in decompensation.
recommendation: Discontinue in decompensated cirrhosis. Statins may be continued in compensated chronic liver disease with monitoring.

condition: Active liver disease / personal or family history
mechanism: Idiosyncratic hepatotoxicity; mitochondrial dysfunction.
recommendation: Avoid in active liver disease; baseline LFTs before initiation; suspicion of hepatic disorder mandates withdrawal.

mechanism: Additive hepatotoxicity.
recommendation: Modified TB regimen (e.g. omitting pyrazinamide) with intensive LFT monitoring per WHO; specialist input.

references.label: WHO TB guidance; ATS hepatotoxicity statement

mechanism: Hepatotoxicity; impaired metabolism.
recommendation: Reduce dose with intensive LFT and FBC monitoring; assess risk-benefit.

mechanism: Hepatic metabolism; nephrotoxicity worsens with hepatorenal physiology.
recommendation: Reduce dose; TDM-guided; specialist input.

mechanism: Hepatic metabolism; reduced clearance.
recommendation: Reduce starting dose; TDM-guided.

mechanism: Therapeutic use: reduce portal pressure; risks include hypotension, AKI in advanced decompensation.
recommendation: Use propranolol/carvedilol per Baveno consensus; withhold during refractory ascites, SBP, hypotension, AKI; reassess.

condition: Active liver disease / severe cirrhosis / liver tumour
mechanism: Hepatic adenoma association; hepatic metabolism; coagulopathy.
recommendation: Avoid CHC in active hepatitis, severe cirrhosis, hepatic adenoma, HCC. Progestogen-only methods preferred.

mechanism: Cholestatic hepatitis reported.
recommendation: Avoid erythromycin estolate; use azithromycin alternative.

mechanism: Cholestatic DILI risk especially with prolonged courses, elderly, HLA-B*57:01.
recommendation: Limit course to ≤14 days; avoid in patients with prior flucloxacillin DILI; counsel on hepatic symptoms.

mechanism: Hepatotoxicity (steatosis, hepatitis, cirrhosis).
recommendation: Baseline LFTs; 6-monthly monitoring; discontinue if ALT >3× ULN persistently.

mechanism: Non-selective beta-blockade precipitates bronchospasm.
recommendation: Avoid sotalol; use class III alternative (amiodarone) or rate control.

mechanism: Systemic absorption can trigger bronchospasm even from eye drops.
recommendation: Avoid in asthma; use prostaglandin analogue or alpha-2 agonist for IOP control.

mechanism: COX-1 inhibition shunts arachidonate to leukotrienes provoking severe bronchospasm in susceptible asthmatics with nasal polyps.
recommendation: Avoid all NSAIDs; paracetamol generally tolerated; selective COX-2 may be tolerated under specialist guidance.

mechanism: Cardioselectivity is dose-dependent; high doses can provoke bronchospasm in severe disease.
recommendation: Selective beta-blockers acceptable in mild-moderate asthma when essential (e.g. post-MI); avoid or use lowest dose with specialist input in severe asthma.

mechanism: Bradykinin accumulation causes dry persistent cough in 5-20% of patients.
recommendation: If troublesome, switch to ARB (does not affect bradykinin).

mechanism: Histamine release (with morphine) and respiratory depression; risk of bronchospasm.
recommendation: Use fentanyl or other non-histamine-releasing opioid in severe asthma; monitor respiratory status.

mechanism: Cardioselective beta-blockers generally safe in stable COPD and improve cardiovascular outcomes; non-selective agents should be avoided.
recommendation: Use cardioselective beta-blocker (bisoprolol, metoprolol succinate) when cardiovascular indication; avoid non-selective.

mechanism: Mask adrenergic warning symptoms of hypoglycaemia (tremor, tachycardia); diaphoresis preserved.
recommendation: Counsel on glucose monitoring and atypical hypoglycaemia symptoms; cardioselective preferred when needed.

mechanism: Increase hepatic gluconeogenesis and peripheral insulin resistance → hyperglycaemia, sometimes HHS.
recommendation: Anticipate dose increases of insulin/oral agents during steroid courses; monitor glucose 4× daily during high-dose courses.

mechanism: Marked weight gain, dyslipidaemia, hyperglycaemia.
recommendation: Avoid as first-line in metabolic syndrome / diabetes; consider aripiprazole or other lower-risk agent; baseline + 3-monthly metabolic monitoring.

mechanism: Marked weight gain and insulin resistance.
recommendation: Continue if clinically essential (treatment-resistant schizophrenia); intensified glucose, lipid, weight monitoring.

mechanism: Dose-related impaired glucose tolerance and hypokalaemia-worsened glycaemia.
recommendation: Use low-dose thiazide-like agents (indapamide, chlortalidone) at standard antihypertensive doses; monitor glucose.

mechanism: Reports of severe hypoglycaemia and hyperglycaemia; mechanism includes effect on KATP channels and pancreatic islet function.
recommendation: Use with caution; counsel on glucose monitoring; choose alternative antibiotic where possible.

mechanism: Calcineurin inhibitors are diabetogenic, especially tacrolimus.
recommendation: Monitor fasting glucose / HbA1c post-transplant; consider tacrolimus minimisation or ciclosporin switch in NODAT.

mechanism: Insulin resistance and dyslipidaemia.
recommendation: Monitor metabolic profile; prefer integrase inhibitor-based regimens where appropriate.

condition: Severe peripheral arterial disease / critical limb ischaemia
mechanism: Historically cautioned for limb perfusion; current evidence supports cardioselective use when indicated.
recommendation: Cardioselective beta-blocker acceptable in most PAD; avoid in critical limb ischaemia with rest pain.

mechanism: Lowers seizure threshold (especially with SSRIs, MAOIs).
recommendation: Avoid in uncontrolled epilepsy; use alternative analgesic (codeine, oxycodone) if opioid needed.

mechanism: Pro-convulsant especially at supratherapeutic levels.
recommendation: TDM-guided; consider alternative bronchodilator strategy.

mechanism: GABA-A antagonism lowers seizure threshold.
recommendation: Avoid in epilepsy where alternative effective antibiotic exists; counsel on seizure warning.

mechanism: Dose-related seizure risk (1-5% at higher doses).
recommendation: Slow titration; consider AED prophylaxis at higher doses; specialist supervision.

mechanism: Carbapenems (especially imipenem) lower seizure threshold.
recommendation: Prefer meropenem (lower seizure liability) in CNS infection or epilepsy.

mechanism: Pro-convulsant in overdose and in susceptible patients.
recommendation: Avoid in epilepsy; use alternative NSAID or paracetamol.

mechanism: Carbapenems dramatically lower valproate levels causing breakthrough seizures.
recommendation: Avoid carbapenem co-prescription; use alternative antibiotic or supplement AED cover.

mechanism: Pupillary dilatation precipitates angle closure.
recommendation: Avoid in known narrow-angle disease; ophthalmology liaison for essential use.

mechanism: Anticholinergic mydriasis precipitates closure.
recommendation: Avoid; consider beta-3 agonist (mirabegron) alternative.

mechanism: Anticholinergic mydriasis.

recommendation: Use lowest dose; monitor for retention; catheterise if needed.

mechanism: Anticholinergic effects on bladder.
recommendation: Use second-generation antihistamine alternatives.

mechanism: Oxidant haemolysis from sulphonamide component.

mechanism: Severe acute haemolytic anaemia.

recommendation: Absolutely contraindicated; use allopurinol with hyperhydration for tumour lysis prophylaxis.

recommendation: Low-dose antiplatelet (75 mg) is generally safe; avoid high anti-inflammatory doses.

mechanism: Oxidant haemolysis reported.
recommendation: Use with caution; alternative antimicrobials preferred for non-critical infections.

mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition raises statin exposure causing rhabdomyolysis.
recommendation: Avoid simvastatin/lovastatin; use atorvastatin (low dose), rosuvastatin or pravastatin.

recommendation: Switch to rifabutin where feasible; adjust dolutegravir to 50 mg BD; consult HIV pharmacist.

mechanism: NNRTI induction reduces methadone levels precipitating withdrawal.
recommendation: Anticipate methadone dose increase (often 25-50%) on starting efavirenz; specialist OST input.

mechanism: Gastric pH increase reduces antiretroviral absorption to subtherapeutic levels.
recommendation: Avoid PPIs with rilpivirine; with atazanavir, follow strict timing per label or switch antacid strategy.

mechanism: Proximal tubular toxicity / Fanconi syndrome; bone demineralisation.
recommendation: Avoid TDF in eGFR <50 where possible; switch to tenofovir alafenamide (TAF) or alternative NRTI.

mechanism: Steroids can precipitate mania, psychosis, depression — risk dose-dependent.
recommendation: Counsel before high-dose courses; consider psychiatric review; taper rather than abrupt stop where possible.

mechanism: Reports of mood disturbance and suicidality; causality debated.
recommendation: Counsel patients and families; baseline mental-health assessment; monitor and stop if mood deterioration.

mechanism: Initial reports of neuropsychiatric events; EAGLES trial reassuring but vigilance recommended.
recommendation: Use with monitoring; advise patient/family to report mood/behaviour changes.

mechanism: Risk of manic switch; particularly without mood stabiliser cover.
recommendation: Avoid antidepressant monotherapy; co-prescribe mood stabiliser; specialist input.

mechanism: Neuropsychiatric ADRs (anxiety, depression, psychosis); seizure risk.
recommendation: Avoid mefloquine in psychiatric or seizure history; use alternative malaria prophylaxis (doxycycline, atovaquone-proguanil).

mechanism: Strongly associated with depression and suicidality.
recommendation: Baseline psychiatric assessment; close monitoring; SSRI prophylaxis considered.

mechanism: Mood / behavioural ADRs including irritability, depression, suicidality.
recommendation: Counsel patient and family; monitor mood; switch to brivaracetam or alternative AED if intolerable.

recommendation: Caution with LQTS; avoid concomitant QT-prolonging drugs; CYP3A4 inhibition raises statin/colchicine levels.

condition: Long QT syndrome / risk of QT prolongation

recommendation: Dose-related QT effect, especially at >400 mg/day; ECG monitoring in high-risk patients.

condition: Long QT syndrome / risk of QT prolongation

recommendation: Among QT-active fluoroquinolones; avoid with LQTS or concurrent QT-prolonging drugs.

recommendation: Pharmacological QT prolongation expected; baseline and surveillance ECG; correct K/Mg.

recommendation: Dose-related QT prolongation and torsades; in-hospital initiation with telemetry.

condition: Long QT syndrome / risk of QT prolongation

recommendation: Restrict use; avoid in QT prolongation, electrolyte disturbance, hepatic impairment; max 30 mg/day, ≤7 days.

mechanism: Antiplatelet effect, GI mucosal injury and protein-binding interactions raise major bleeding risk.
recommendation: Avoid NSAID + oral anticoagulant; if essential add PPI gastroprotection and limit duration.

mechanism: Reduced platelet serotonin uptake impairs aggregation, particularly raising upper-GI bleed risk with anticoagulant.
recommendation: Add PPI gastroprotection in high-risk patients; consider alternative antidepressant (mirtazapine).

mechanism: Increase mucosal vulnerability and INR variability.
recommendation: Add gastroprotection; monitor INR closely; minimise duration.

mechanism: Combination antiplatelet+anticoagulant markedly increases bleeding.
recommendation: Limit duration of triple/dual therapy after PCI; reassess regularly; PPI cover.

mechanism: Possible impaired calcium absorption; FDA labelled fracture risk with prolonged high-dose use.
recommendation: Use lowest effective dose; review need annually; ensure calcium/vitamin D adequacy.

mechanism: Associated with reduced BMD and falls/fractures in elderly observational data.
recommendation: Weigh against depression risk; falls prevention measures; consider mirtazapine alternative in frail elderly.

mechanism: Suppress osteoblast function and accelerate bone loss; fracture risk rises within months.
recommendation: Initiate bone protection (calcium, vitamin D, bisphosphonate) per NOGG guidance in patients on ≥3 months prednisolone ≥7.5 mg.

mechanism: Profound oestrogen suppression accelerates bone loss.
recommendation: Baseline + 2-yearly DEXA; bisphosphonate per ABS; calcium/vitamin D supplementation.

mechanism: Androgen / oestrogen deprivation accelerates bone loss.
recommendation: Baseline DEXA and bone protection counselling; bisphosphonate if high fracture risk.

mechanism: Bone loss from androgen deprivation.
recommendation: Bone protection per oncology guidance.

mechanism: Reduces BMD especially in adolescents and women approaching menopause; partly reversible.
recommendation: Counsel on BMD effect; review continuation every 2 years; consider alternative LARC where appropriate.

mechanism: Sympathomimetic effects can precipitate or worsen tachyarrhythmias.
recommendation: Avoid in significant arrhythmia / structural heart disease; cardiology screening before initiation.

mechanism: Tachycardia and arrhythmia risk at high doses; hypokalaemia compounds.
recommendation: Avoid excess dosing; check K+ during heavy nebuliser use.

mechanism: Subclinical / overt hyperthyroidism precipitates AF, especially in elderly.
recommendation: Maintain TSH within reference range; avoid TSH-suppressive doses outside oncology indication.

mechanism: Additive vasoconstriction; risk of severe ischaemia.
recommendation: Avoid combination; separate by at least 24 h (or longer per agent).

mechanism: Combined serotonergic action; clinical syndrome rare in modern data.
recommendation: Counsel on serotonin syndrome features; continue both where indicated; review if features develop.

mechanism: Increased ischaemic stroke risk in migraine with aura.
recommendation: Use progestogen-only or non-hormonal methods; migraine with aura is UKMEC 4.

mechanism: Bleeding risk during/after surgery.
recommendation: Stop 24-48 h before low-bleed-risk surgery; 48-96 h for high-bleed-risk or impaired renal function; resume 24-72 h post-op based on haemostasis.

mechanism: Bleeding risk; need for bridging if high thrombotic risk.
recommendation: Stop 5 days pre-op; bridge with LMWH if mechanical valve / recent VTE / high CHA2DS2-VASc; resume within 24 h post-op per haemostasis.

mechanism: Bleeding versus thrombotic risk balance; POISE-2 data inform decisions.
recommendation: Continue aspirin for secondary prevention through most surgery; stop 7 days pre-op only in high-bleed-risk procedures (intracranial, spinal).

mechanism: Significant bleeding risk; balanced against stent thrombosis.
recommendation: Stop clopidogrel 5 days, prasugrel 7 days, ticagrelor 3-5 days before high-bleed-risk surgery; discuss timing with cardiology.

mechanism: Delayed gastric emptying raises aspiration risk during anaesthesia.
recommendation: Consider holding weekly GLP-1 RA on the day of surgery (and the week prior); follow ASA guidance; treat as full stomach if not held.

references.label: ASA guidance on GLP-1 RA perioperative

mechanism: Risk of euglycaemic DKA, especially with fasting/illness.
recommendation: Hold for 3 days before major surgery (4 days for ertugliflozin); check ketones; resume when eating normally.

mechanism: Lactic acidosis risk if AKI develops.
recommendation: Hold metformin on day of contrast/surgery if eGFR <60 or contrast >100 mL; restart at 48 h with recheck of renal function.

mechanism: Hypotension under anaesthesia; AKI risk.
recommendation: Omit on morning of surgery; restart within 24-48 h when haemodynamically stable.

mechanism: Increased BP/HR; reports of sudden death in structural cardiac disease.
recommendation: Cardiology evaluation (ECG ± echo) before initiation in known heart disease, syncope, family sudden death history.

mechanism: Modest BP/HR increase.
recommendation: Baseline BP/HR; monitor; specialist review before in serious cardiovascular disease.

mechanism: Dopamine D2 blockade worsens motor symptoms.
recommendation: Avoid; use quetiapine or clozapine for psychosis in PD.

mechanism: Severe neuroleptic sensitivity — irreversible parkinsonism, autonomic instability, NMS.
recommendation: Avoid where possible; quetiapine lowest dose with caution; non-pharmacological strategies first.

mechanism: May worsen neuromuscular transmission.
recommendation: Use with caution; close clinical monitoring; alternative mood stabiliser preferred.

mechanism: Block neuromuscular transmission; may precipitate crisis.
recommendation: Avoid; alternative antibiotic; if essential, monitor respiratory status closely.

mechanism: May worsen muscle weakness.
recommendation: Use with monitoring; consider alternative.

mechanism: Impairs neuromuscular transmission.
recommendation: Avoid IV magnesium where alternative exists; monitor respiratory function if used.

mechanism: Falls, fractures, delirium, cognitive impairment.
recommendation: Avoid long-acting benzodiazepines; if needed use short-acting agent (lorazepam) at lowest dose, short duration.

mechanism: Falls and confusion risk.
recommendation: Avoid where possible; non-pharmacological sleep approaches; if used, lowest dose, brief duration.

recommendation: Avoid TCAs in elderly; prefer SSRI/mirtazapine.

recommendation: Use second-generation antihistamines.

recommendation: Use lowest effective dose (typically 62.5-125 µg); avoid >125 µg/day in elderly unless TDM justifies.

recommendation: Avoid in pregnancy; effective contraception both partners; switch to azathioprine pre-conception in transplant/lupus.

mechanism: Severe limb / cardiac teratogenicity.
recommendation: Pregnancy Prevention Programme; absolute contraindication.

recommendation: Avoid in pregnancy.

condition: Risk of severe bradycardia / heart block

recommendation: Avoid; treat insomnia non-pharmacologically; optimise CPAP.

recommendation: Calculate ACB score; deprescribe; substitute non-anticholinergic alternatives.

mechanism: Reduced renal clearance.

recommendation: Suspend simvastatin / atorvastatin during short courses (e.g. 7 days clarithromycin); avoid simvastatin >40 mg with strong inhibitors.

condition: Risk of tendon rupture / aortic aneurysm

recommendation: Glucagon IV adjunct considered in beta-blocker-related refractory anaphylaxis; continue beta-blocker decision case-by-case.

recommendation: Avoid combination; if essential lowest doses, counsel on overdose, consider naloxone supply.

recommendation: Suspend simvastatin during clarithromycin course; azithromycin is the lowest-risk macrolide.

recommendation: Halve digoxin dose when starting amiodarone; check level at steady state.

mechanism: Possible inhibition of warfarin metabolism reported.
recommendation: Counsel on consistent intake; INR monitoring if intake changes.

mechanism: Enzyme induction reduces warfarin levels.
recommendation: Counsel against St John's wort; INR monitoring if started/stopped.

mechanism: Additive vasodilatation.
recommendation: Stable alpha-blocker therapy first; lowest PDE-5 inhibitor dose; tamsulosin lower interaction risk than non-selective.

mechanism: Drive K+ intracellularly; potentiated by xanthines, diuretics, steroids.
recommendation: Monitor K+ during severe asthma / nebulised treatment; replace as needed.

condition: Risk of toxicity from electrolyte shifts

recommendation: Consider holding 24 h before major surgery; monitor levels post-operatively.

mechanism: Sustained paracetamol use modestly raises INR.
recommendation: Consistent dose; check INR after starting regular paracetamol; lowest effective dose.

mechanism: Pethidine + MAOI causes severe hypertension, hyperthermia, coma.
recommendation: Avoid pethidine, tramadol, methadone with MAOIs; morphine generally considered safer with caution.

mechanism: CYP2D6 inhibition raises metoprolol levels.
recommendation: Choose non-CYP2D6 SSRI (sertraline/citalopram) or use bisoprolol; monitor HR.

mechanism: Additive bleeding via platelet serotonin depletion; some SSRIs also raise INR.
recommendation: Monitor for bleeding; consider PPI gastroprotection; mirtazapine alternative where appropriate.

mechanism: Preload reduction may cause severe hypotension and syncope.
recommendation: Use with caution and slow titration; specialist input for symptomatic severe AS.

mechanism: Preload reduction may compromise stroke volume.
recommendation: Use lowest effective dose; cautious diuresis with monitoring.

condition: Pre-existing vestibular dysfunction / sensorineural hearing loss
mechanism: Cochlear and vestibular ototoxicity.
recommendation: Avoid where possible; audiometric monitoring during essential courses; TDM.

mechanism: Synergistic cochlear damage.
recommendation: Avoid combination; if essential lowest doses with audiometric monitoring.

mechanism: Risk of NMS or worsening catatonia.
recommendation: Avoid; benzodiazepines and ECT are first-line; specialist guidance.

mechanism: Respiratory depression raises CO2 → ICP; clinical assessment obscured.
recommendation: Cautious analgesia in monitored setting; intubation/ventilation considered for safe analgesia.

mechanism: Possible association with mood disturbance; signal weak.
recommendation: Use lowest effective dose; consider bisoprolol if beta-blocker required.
